title: Geometric stalk of underived proper-support direct image
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $f:X\to Y$ a separated morphism locally of finite type of schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose $G\subseteq f_*F$ is a subsheaf [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] such that, for each etale $V\to Y$, $G(V)$ consists exactly of the sections of $F(X\times_YV)$ whose closed support, defined by nonzero geometric germs [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], is proper over $V$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $X_{\bar y}=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with projection $a_{\bar y}:X_{\bar y}\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $H^0_c(X_{\bar y},a_{\bar y}^{-1}F)$ for the submodule of $\Gamma(X_{\bar y},a_{\bar y}^{-1}F)$ consisting of sections whose closed support is proper over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Restricting a representative section $s\in G(V)$ along $X_{\bar y}\to X\times_YV$ induces a $\Lambda$-linear isomorphism
$$G_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0_c(X_{\bar y},a_{\bar y}^{-1}F),$$
natural in $F$. Its composite with the inclusion into $\Gamma(X_{\bar y},a_{\bar y}^{-1}F)$ equals the ordinary restriction map from the submodule $G_{\bar y}\subseteq(f_*F)_{\bar y}$.

source.place: Tag 0F76 (lemma-stalk-f-shriek-separated), including the precise description of c_y in the first two paragraphs of its proof; module version obtained by keeping the scalar actions on restriction maps

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], a germ in $G_{\bar y}$ has a representative $s\in G(V)$ on a pointed etale neighbourhood. Restrict it to $X_{\bar y}$. The germ compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] shows that the nonzero-germ locus of the restricted section is precisely the inverse image of the support of $s$. By clause (1) of [lem-cbc-closed-proper-support-locality] this support is proper over $\Omega$. Restriction commutes with refinement of the neighbourhood, so it induces a well-defined homomorphism $c:G_{\bar y}\to H^0_c(X_{\bar y},a_{\bar y}^{-1}F)$. Every restriction is $\Lambda$-linear, so $c$ is too. Exactness of the geometric stalk functor [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identifies the stalk of the given subsheaf with a submodule of $(f_*F)_{\bar y}$; by its construction, $c$ followed by inclusion is exactly ordinary restriction.

For an open $U\subset X$, let $P_U(V)$ be the set of proper-support sections on $U_V$ and take its pointed-neighbourhood colimit as a set of germs. Base-change properness in [lem-cbc-closed-proper-support-locality] and step 1 make these restriction maps well-defined. We record explicitly the open-extension argument used below (Tag 0F53, remark-covariance-f-shriek-separated). If $U\subset X$ is open and $s$ is a section of $F|_U$ on $U_V$ with support $C$ proper over $V$, give $C$ its reduced structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The triangle $C\to X_V\to V$ has proper composite and separated second map: $X_V\to V$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] applied to $f$. By [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target], $C\to X_V$ is proper, hence has closed image by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its image is the same reduced closed subscheme as $C$ (this is checked on the open $U_V$ containing it). Glue $s$ on $U_V$ to zero on $X_V\setminus C$: they agree on $U_V\setminus C$ since every germ there is zero, so [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open] says that the restriction there is zero. Sheaf separation and gluing are those of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Sheaf gluing gives a unique section on $X_V$ with support $C$. It lies in $G(V)$. This operation is injective, commutes with restriction, and hence defines an injection from the pointed colimit of $P_U$ into $G_{\bar y}$: if two extended representatives agree after a refinement, their restrictions to $U$ agree after that same refinement, which is the equality criterion of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Over $\Omega$, [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] applied to $f$ makes $X_{\bar y}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ separated, so the triangle $C\to X_{\bar y}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ again has proper composite and separated second map, so $C$ is closed in $X_{\bar y}$. Glue the section on $U_{\bar y}$ to zero off $C$; restriction back to $U_{\bar y}$ is a left inverse, giving an injection on compactly supported fibre sections. The square with the restriction maps $c$ commutes: both paths restrict $s$ on the open and are zero on its complement, and gluing is unique.

source.place: Tags 0F53 and 0F74 (remark-covariance-f-shriek-separated and remark-covariance-compact-support); Tag 0F76 open-subscheme square

proof.text: We may restrict $Y$ to an affine open containing the image of $\bar y$: pointed neighbourhoods mapping into it are cofinal, since one can intersect any pointed neighbourhood with its inverse image. Suppose $s\in G_{\bar y}$ is in the kernel of $c$. Represent it on an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $V$ (shrink around its marked point). Its support $C$ is proper over affine $V$, so is quasi-compact by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its image in $X$ is quasi-compact, so finitely many affine opens of $X$ cover that image; their union is a quasi-compact open $U$. The section is the extension of its restriction to $U_V$ by step 2. The corresponding fibre section on $U_{\bar y}$ is zero, because the fibre extension is injective. Consequently injectivity of the map from the pointed colimit of $P_U$ for every quasi-compact open $U\subset X$ implies injectivity for $X$. For surjectivity, the support of any $t\in H^0_c(X_{\bar y},a_{\bar y}^{-1}F)$ is quasi-compact. Cover its image in $X$ by finitely many affine opens and let $U$ be their union. Its restriction to $U_{\bar y}$ retains the same proper support, and step 2 extends it back to $t$. Surjectivity from the pointed colimit of $P_U$ therefore gives surjectivity for $X$. Here the finite subcovers and finite unions are elementary quasi-compactness arguments using the affine-open basis of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]; no quasi-compactness of the original $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F76, affine-base reduction and the two quasi-compact-open reductions

proof.text: It remains to prove bijectivity when $Y$ is affine and $X$ is quasi-compact. For this reduced case use $P_X$ in place of the originally given $G$; step 5 identifies it with a sheaf, so its pointed colimit is a stalk. Since $f$ is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, it is finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The affine scheme $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] and [def-nagata-compactification] to obtain $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, with $j$ an open immersion and $p$ proper. Work with the underlying abelian sheaf of $F$ and put $H=j_!F$. Its restriction to $X$ is $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso], and its stalks outside $X$ are zero by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks].

Restriction identifies the presheaf $P_X$ with $p_*H$, and thus with $G$ whenever the latter is given. Indeed, for etale $V\to Y$, a section of $H$ on $\overline X_V$ has closed support by [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open] (its complement is the zero-germ open), and that support is disjoint from $\overline X_V\setminus X_V$, by the zero stalks in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks] and the germ formula [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. The support is proper over $V$: $\overline X_V\to V$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and its reduced closed support is proper by clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Thus its restriction is in $P_X(V)$. Conversely, given $s\in P_X(V)$, its support $C$ is closed also in $\overline X_V$ by the proper-triangle argument of step 2. Use [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso] to view $s$ as a section of $H$ on $X_V$, and glue it to zero on $\overline X_V\setminus C$. These two constructions are inverse: on $X_V$ they preserve $s$, and off $C$ both sections are zero, with equality checked by applying [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open] to their difference, followed by sheaf separation [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. They commute with etale restriction and with morphisms of $F$, since restriction and gluing do. This proves the sheaf identification of Tag 0F52 without invoking the composition node (which depends on our item).

On the geometric fibre, [sbc-prop-extension-by-zero-and-arbitrary-base-change] identifies $H|_{\overline X_{\bar y}}$ with $j_{\bar y,!}(F|_{X_{\bar y}})$. Over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, the construction is as follows: using [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso] and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], sections on the proper $\overline X_{\bar y}$ have closed support by [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open], contained inside $X_{\bar y}$; properness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Conversely, let $t$ be a compactly supported section with reduced support $C$. The triangle $C\to\overline X_{\bar y}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has proper composite and separated second map, so [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] makes $C\to\overline X_{\bar y}$ proper and its image closed. Regard $t$ as a section of the pulled-back $H$ on $X_{\bar y}$ using the unit isomorphism, and glue it to zero on $\overline X_{\bar y}\setminus C$. On the intersection it is zero by [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open]; sheaf gluing [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] gives the extension. Restriction is a left inverse. It is also a right inverse because the difference from the original section has zero germs both on $X_{\bar y}$ and off $C$, so the zero-open node makes it zero. We obtain $\Gamma(\overline X_{\bar y},H|_{\overline X_{\bar y}})\cong H^0_c(X_{\bar y},F|_{X_{\bar y}})$. For a representative $s\in G(V)$, its extension to $H(\overline X_V)$ pulls back to a section whose restriction to $X_{\bar y}$ is $s|_{X_{\bar y}}$ and whose restriction off the pulled-back support is zero. Uniqueness of the same gluing proves that this identification commutes with the actual restriction maps, not merely that the two objects are abstractly isomorphic.

source.place: Tag 0F75 (lemma-compactify-compact-support) and the final commutative square in Tag 0F76

proof.text: For the proper $p$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-geometric-point-exchange] gives an isomorphism $\bar y^{-1}p_*H\to p_{\bar y,*}(H|_{\overline X_{\bar y}})$ with no torsion hypothesis. By [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], the exchange is adjoint to pushforward of the inverse-image unit, so on a representative section it sends $s$ to its pullback on the fibre. Taking sections on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and using [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] identifies it with the canonical restriction $(p_*H)_{\bar y}\to\Gamma(\overline X_{\bar y},H|_{\overline X_{\bar y}})$. By steps 5 and 6 this is precisely $c$. Thus $c$ is bijective in the quasi-compact case, and step 3 proves it in general. Finally for any $\Lambda$-linear map $F\to F'$, the support of the image of a section is closed by [lem-sc-etale-section-zero-open] and contained in its old support, since a linear map sends a zero germ to zero; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] preserves properness, so the map restricts to proper-support sections. Both composites in the naturality square send a representative $s$ to the restriction of its image, proving naturality. Since $c$ is already $\Lambda$-linear by step 1, its inverse is $\Lambda$-linear as well: apply injectivity to $c(\lambda c^{-1}(t))=\lambda t$.
